title: Strata Tiles: multi-granularity performance tiles for model & route overview
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Overview: Design a compact, information-dense "strata" tile system for Redwood Console that combines per-route and per-model performance signals (latency, throughput, token metrics, and cost) into interactive micro-tiles. Goal is to provide product and infra engineers a single glance-and-drill UX: glance for SLO violations and cost spikes; drill for token-level traces and request samples.

Problem statement: Current model/route pages are a mix of large charts and lists. Teams ask for a compact dashboard that can be embedded in high-level views (project/stack dashboard) while still supporting fast deep-dive workflows. We need tiles that are legible at three sizes (compact list, medium panel, expanded detail) and that surface both statistical summaries and examples.

Proposed solution summary: "Strata Tiles" are modular UI tiles built from three stacked bands (summary ribbon, stability glyph, and micro-chart). Each tile supports three granularities: "micro" (single-line compact), "panel" (normal), and "detail" (expands inline). Data surfaced: median latency, p95, p99, request/sec, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and a sample request link. Visual language: low-ink ribbon for percentiles with an overlaid jitter band, a mini-sparkline for throughput with a rolling median band, and a density strip for token-size distribution. Interactions: hover reveals precise numbers, click toggles expansion, and a secondary click opens token-waterfall microtrace in the Console drawer.

Chart & component specs (high-level):
- Aggregation tiers: default 5m rollup with options 1m and 1h. All tiles lazy-load raw microtrace data on expansion only.
- Percentile ribbon: renders median as a center line, p50/p75/p90 as graduated shaded bands, and p99 as a thin upper whisker. The ribbon includes a translucent "jitter" overlay (max-min band) accessible via toggle for low-noise workloads.
- Throughput micro-chart: 1-row sparkline (height ~24px) with two layers: rolling median (thicker line) and per-bucket bars (thin stroke). Tooltip shows request count and tokens in bucket.
- Token density strip: 6-color gradient strip representing token-count percentiles; clicking opens histogram modal with bucket counts and sample normalized prompts.
- Cost badge: micro-badge top-right showing cost per 1k tokens; color-coded by change vs baseline (green/neutral/red).
- Sample-request affordance: small chevron that opens a sampled request panel with anonymized input/output and latency trace.

Accessibility & performance constraints:
- High-contrast mode: ensure badges and ribbons meet WCAG AA for text and 3:1 for icons where possible. Provide an alternative compressed text view for low-vision users.
- Reduced motion: animated jitter overlays and sparkline transitions must respect reduced-motion setting.
- Telemetry cost: microtraces and token histograms are sampled; default sampling 1% for heavy routes, 10% for routes flagged by alerts. This is a backend constraint coordinated with Eng.

Prototype notes:
- Figma prototype includes three tile sizes in a sample project dashboard, and an inline expansion animation showing the token waterfall drawer and histogram modal.
- Interaction flow: tile hover -> quick actions (view samples, pin tile, set alert) -> click -> expand -> draw microtrace. User testing will validate that expansion is discoverable and that compact tiles are scannable at 1200px width with 12 tiles visible.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Density vs clarity: we chose graduated bands rather than raw error bars to reduce visual noise in compact view. This sacrifices showing full distribution but retains actionability (p50/p90/p99).
- Data freshness vs cost: defaulting to 5-minute rollups reduces backend load, but the detail view allows a manual "live" toggle to stream recent values for debugging.
- Color encoding: avoid heat-only encoding for percentile bands to keep pattern-driven recognition for color-blind users; rely on shape (band width) and labels as well.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- In usability tests (n=6 infra/product engineers) 80% can identify a p99 latency regression and open the sample request trace within 30s.
- Tile scan time (time to first relevant signal) under 5s for dashboards with up to 24 tiles.
- No more than 10% increase in Console page bundle size when deferring microtrace assets to expansion phase.

decision_log: Default aggregation set to 5m to balance freshness and cost.
Percentiles shown: p50 (median), p75, p90, p99. Full distribution available in expanded histogram.
Microtraces and histograms will be sampled server-side; front-end lazy-load on expansion.
Accessiblity: provide high-contrast theme and keyboard-first interactions.
Rendering: prefer canvas for sparkline; SVG for ribbons when expanded for accessibility labels.
Cost badge color rule: >+20% vs baseline = red, -10%..+20% = amber, <-10% = green.
